mdcalc_rules: Five criteria, each scored 1-3. Total bilirubin: <2 mg/dL (<34.2 umol/L) +1, 2-3 mg/dL (34.2-51.3 umol/L) +2, >3 mg/dL (>51.3 umol/L) +3. Albumin: >3.5 g/dL (>35 g/L) +1, 2.8-3.5 g/dL (28-35 g/L) +2, <2.8 g/dL +3. INR: <1.7 +1, 1.7-2.3 +2, >2.3 +3. Ascites: absent +1, slight +2, moderate +3. Encephalopathy: none +1, grade 1-2 +2, grade 3-4 +3. The middle bins include both endpoints, so bili 2.0 or 3.0 = +2, albumin 3.5 or 2.8 = +2, INR 1.7 or 2.3 = +2. Total 5-15 (class A 5-6, B 7-9, C 10-15 by the standard Pugh cutoffs).

code_vs_mdcalc.issue: Bilirubin in umol/L is converted with molar mass 584.66 (1 mg/dL = 17.104 umol/L), not the factor 17.1 that MDCalc's printed cutoffs imply. So exactly 34.2 umol/L becomes 1.9995 mg/dL and scores +1, while MDCalc puts 34.2 umol/L in the 2-3 bin (+2). The upper boundary is unaffected: 51.3 umol/L becomes 2.9993 and scores +2, as on MDCalc. This is an edge case only.

All thresholds, inclusive boundaries, the albumin g/L to g/dL conversion and the defaults (missing ascites = absent +1, missing encephalopathy = none +1) match MDCalc. Minor robustness gaps: INR, bilirubin and albumin are required with no default; an ascites or encephalopathy string outside the expected labels silently adds 0 points; and the ascites 'absent' check reads input_variables['ascites'] directly rather than ascites_state, which is harmless. No stored row hits any of these.
